subject: Urgent: Dedicated pool saturation impacting Checkout API - reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fastcheckout.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: FastCheckout Engineering <eng@fastcheckout.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:12:00Z
Subject: Increasing 429s and timeouts from your dedicated pool (northstar-prod)

Camila,

We started seeing a spike in 429s and p99 latency across our Checkout API at 08:45 PDT this morning. Error rate jumped from ~0.1% to ~3.6% and several transactions are timing out (~20s). Our engineering team traced it to requests being routed to your dedicated GPU pool (northstar-prod) where we are observing queueing and token throttling. This is directly impacting our checkout conversion.

Attached is a short excerpt of the logs and a screenshot of the metrics around the spike. We are on a reserved-capacity contract and were expecting steady throughput for this window. Please advise immediate mitigation and an ETA for a fix.

--
Samir Patel
Head of Engineering
FastCheckout
samir.patel@fastcheckout.com
+1 (415) 555-7910
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fastcheckout.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T09:24:00Z
Subject: Re: Increasing 429s and timeouts from your dedicated pool (northstar-prod)

Samir —

Thanks for the heads up and the artifacts, sorry for the hit to conversion. I’m escalating to our on-call and will get an incident bridge up now. Initial read: reserved pool is showing elevated queue depth and token backpressure; autoscaling attempted but there was an allocation delay for queued shards.

Immediate next steps we are executing now:
- Stand up incident bridge and capture logs (Priyom)
- Apply emergency routing policy to shift low-priority background traffic off your pool (Naomi)
- Evaluate temporary throttle lift for your reserved queue to honor committed throughput (internal ops)

I’ll add you to the bridge and follow up with expected timeline within 30 minutes.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: Incident bridge notes and proposed mitigations for northstar-prod

TL;DR: Dedicated pool northstar-prod saturated at 08:40 PDT. Root contributors: burst of long-sequence generations from a partner integration + KV cache misses after recent model upgrade. Reserved throughput enforcement pushed non-reserved jobs into queue.

What we see (metrics attached):
- Sustained queue depth from 08:40–09:10 with p95 queueing latency > 2s
- 429 surge correlating to token service backpressure (mapping to reserved buckets)
- Autoscaler attempted to add capacity but instance provisioning lagged ~6m due to cloud placement constraints

Immediate mitigations performed (10:00):
1) Applied routing policy to divert non-reserved and smaller-length requests to fallback pooled instances (reduced northstar load by ~35%).
2) Emergency override: temporarily prioritize reserved queue for FastCheckout to avoid further SLA violations.
3) Hot patch: re-enable an earlier quantized kernel path for the updated model variant to reduce per-token latency (rolling restart of 2 nodes).

Requested follow-ups and owner map:
- Naomi: coordinate prioritized routing policy and confirm rollback plan (owner)
- Jonas: validate capacity provisioning logs and open cloud placement ticket (owner)
- Camila: keep FastCheckout updated and manage exec notification if SLA credit remediation is requested

Potential customer-facing positions:
- Short window (30–60m) mitigation and full relief expected within 2 hours if cloud placement allows immediate capacity.
- If provisioning delays persist, offer a temporary rate-limited fallback model (slightly cheaper latency but preserves success rate) and discuss SLA remediation.

Attachments: svc_metrics_snapshot.png, throughput_log_excerpt.txt

--
Priyom Das
SRE, Inference Operations
Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@fastcheckout.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priom.das@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-16T15:40:00Z
Subject: Update: relief applied for northstar-prod; additional remediation and next steps

Samir —

Update from our bridge: we’ve reduced the pressure on your reserved pool and are seeing success rate return to baseline. Timeline & summary:
- 10:00–10:20 PDT: routing policy diversion reduced northstar-prod load by ~35%.
- 10:25 PDT: emergency reserved-queue override reduced 429s for FastCheckout traffic; success rate climbed back to ~99.6%.
- 11:05 PDT: rolled a hot-fix to two nodes to re-enable the lower-latency kernel path; p99 latency improved ~18%.

What we are doing next:
- Jonas to open a cloud placement remediation request to reduce future provisioning lag (target: <120s).
- Naomi will run a short evaluation to recommend model-config and KV cache priming settings for your workload to prevent cache-miss amplified bursts.
- We will provide a formal incident report with timeline, root cause analysis, and the list of mitigations in 48 hours.

Compensation and contract notes:
- Given the customer impact and that you were on reserved capacity, I will open the SLA remediation workflow. If you prefer an immediate credit or a one-time bill adjustment while we complete the RCA, say the word and I’ll prioritize with Finance.

Thanks again for flagging quickly. I’ll keep you looped as we close the RCA.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com
